newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB futures close sharply down.
newsitem.headline: JGB futures close sharply down.

text.p: Key March Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended Friday's Tokyo session sharply lower, as investors sold cash JGBs and non-JGB issues such as debentures, traders said.
The March closed down 0.54 at 124.41. Volume was 41,028 contracts.
"JGBs fell sharply in the afternoon as some large-lot selling of cash JGBs emerged," a trader at a city bank's securities unit said.
Investors were selling cash JGBs to realise profits, traders said.
Economic indicators released this morning had little impact on the JGB market, traders said.
Japan's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate for November fell to 3.3 percent from 3.4 percent in October.
Also, the jobs-to-applicants ratio edged up to 0.74 in November from 0.73 in October.
Tokyo area consumer prices rose 0.2 percent year-on-year in December, after a 0.1 percent rise in November.
Traders said bond market participants usually do not pay that much attention to employment and consumer price data.
The yield of the benchmark cash 182nd JGB stood at 2.540 percent, up from 2.495 percent on Thursday.
Traders expect the JGB market to remain susceptible to swings in the yen and Tokyo stocks.
"There is a strong fear that foreign investors' selling in the new year would lead to a 'triple' weakness of the yen, stocks and bonds," a trader at another city bank's securities unit said.
